## 2026-11-06 — Correcting an expense keeps the books true

- **A-18 (tranche 2) — a corrected expense is reversed then re-posted, through the same poster.** `syncExpenseState` in `server/services/accounting.ts` compares the posted net per account (`SUM(debit - credit)` over the expense's journal lines) with the document as it now stands. When they differ it posts `reversal:<signature>` (the mirror of the posted net) then `corrected:<signature>` (the new state); the signature is a hash of the state's lines, so replaying the same correction creates nothing and two successive corrections produce two distinct pairs with exactly one reversal each. `postDocumentEntry('expense', id)` and `syncAccounting` call this one function, so write-time correction and the sweep cannot diverge. `PATCH /expenses` (`server/routes/operations.ts`) posts the correction at write time. No migration: the schema is untouched.
- **Proof:** `tests/accounting-incremental.test.ts` now has **13 cases**, including a nominal correction (charge 25 860 + VAT 4 140, payable 30 000), two successive corrections with replay (5 entries, net 40 000, replay returns false and adds nothing), an expense changed before the wiring that the sweep corrects once then leaves alone, and a sweep after a write-time correction that creates 0 entries and leaves journal, line count and debit/credit totals identical. Mutation: `syncExpenseState` neutralised with `return false` → **5 of 13 cases fail**. Typecheck clean; full suite **103 files / 793 tests**.
- **Still open in A-18:** the five read routes still sweep with `syncAccounting`; the `journal_synced_at` cursor, bounded catch-up, the `POST /accounting/sync` repair route and the D1 query measurement remain. No performance measurement was run.
